name: Pagination
summary: The footer under a long table: how many rows are showing, rows per page, and previous, next and page numbers that collapse to "Page 3 of 49" when narrow.
a11y: A navigation landmark named Pagination; the current page has aria-current, page buttons have full names, the ellipsis is hidden from screen readers and the row count is a polite live region.

use_when: under a list or search results long enough to split, where people need to know how many items there are and jump to a page
avoid_when: a feed people scroll through without needing a page number: load more at the end instead
moving between steps of one task: use setup-steps
switching between views of one page: use page-header-tabs

parts.name: count
parts.what: which rows are showing out of how many

parts.name: rows_per_page
parts.what: a choice of how many rows each page shows

parts.name: previous
parts.what: Previous and Next buttons either side of the pages

parts.name: pages
parts.what: one page number; the current one is marked

parts.name: gap
parts.what: an ellipsis where page numbers are skipped

parts.name: page_of
parts.what: 'Page 3 of 49', shown instead of the numbers when narrow

empty.how: the Smart UI renderer puts one plain 'Nothing to show yet.' line in an empty list

loading.how: the Smart UI renderer draws each marked slot as a quiet block of its size while the data arrives; the static file shows the filled part

error.how: if a page fails to load, stay on the current page and show the reason in alert-banners above the table

disabled.how: a disabled Previous or Next turns grey with a not-allowed cursor, for the first and last page; the sample shows page 3, so neither is disabled

overflow.how: under 900px the page numbers give way to 'Page 3 of 49'; under 520px the count and the pager each take a full row

long_text.how: the count, the rows label and 'Page 3 of 49' never wrap; the bar wraps its groups instead

keyboard: Tab reaches the rows-per-page choice, Previous, each page number, then Next
Arrow keys change the rows-per-page choice, as in any native select
Enter or Space presses the focused button; the file has no script, so pages do not change until the project wires them
